status: Post-execution route-oracle adjudication; implementation and observed outputs remain uninspected by this author.

summary.conclusion: Annual state natural-gas requests do not require Domestic exclusively. Accept Domestic or SEDS when the requested specificity, quantities, geography, frequency, units, and disclosed coverage are preserved. An empty explicit daily Wyoming coal request does not establish a route correctness failure.

scope: Only the disputed route claims in cases 01, 09, 10, 19, 22, 25, 26, 30, 35, 38, and 41 are adjudicated. Other frozen expectations are unchanged. The original cases are exposed regressions, not untouched holdouts.
requirementsBasis: Scope and product coverage determine routing; requested specificity and units cannot be silently substituted.
Unstated frequency means annual with explicit=false and no invented sector.
Explicit unavailable frequency requests may correctly yield no result; alternatives must be visibly labeled.

Approved route profiles include annual Domestic metadata and stateAnnualConceptHints consumption/production for SEDS; stateNonAnnualPrimary Domestic is a routing preference, not proof of product availability.

claims.reasoning: Both families contain annual Texas marketed-natural-gas production in million cubic feet. The explicit marketed qualifier is preserved by SEDS NGMPP and NGMPB; the Domestic-only oracle is unsupported.

Preserve the requested product/activity and any explicit qualifier. A conversion-factor, per-capita, pipeline-fuel-consumption, or natural-gas-liquids record cannot silently stand in for a production or aggregate-consumption quantity.

claims.reasoning: This case also requests electricity generation. Domestic has an all-fuels, all-sectors Texas net-generation series as well as natural-gas production/consumption. The inspected SEDS Texas generation titles cover particular renewable/nuclear fuels and sector subsets, and provide no all-fuels total-generation series. An exclusive SEDS search would therefore restrict the electricity-generation choice. A composite route using SEDS for gas and Domestic for electricity is also acceptable.

Fuel consumed for generation is an input quantity, not generated electricity, and cannot replace the generation pair.
availabilityOrSpecificityConsequences: SEDS-only candidate coverage lacks the inspected all-fuels, all-sectors electricity-generation alternative available as ELEC.GEN.ALL-TX-99.A. Selecting only a renewable/nuclear subset would silently narrow the broad electricity request unless presented as a limited alternative.

claims.reasoning: The query requests daily Wyoming coal production. SEDS is annual only; Domestic is configured as stateNonAnnualPrimary but its cached products are electricity/natural gas. Neither inspected family contains the requested daily coal series. An explicit empty result is semantically correct from either routing policy. The original SEDS-only assertion conflated the available annual coal family with the requested unavailable daily series.
acceptedSemanticCriteria: Keep Wyoming WY, coal production, frequency=daily, explicit=true, and no requested sector.
An empty result must explain that the requested daily series is unavailable in the supported metadata; do not claim coal production does not exist.
Do not silently return or relabel annual SEDS data as daily, and do not replace coal production with coal used for electricity generation.
If an annual alternative is offered, its annual frequency and SEDS source must be explicit and the original daily request must remain unchanged.

This route adjudication does not extend any application policy that permits automatic annual fallback only for monthly/quarterly requests; daily fallback need not be offered and is not needed to pass this case.
availabilityOrSpecificityConsequences: SEDS contains annual Wyoming coal production in thousand short tons and Billion Btu through 2024. An empty daily result does not lose an available daily series.

claims.reasoning: The approved vocabulary uses pipeline as context to resolve ambiguous gas to natural gas. It does not define pipeline as a mandatory production subtype or sector. Neither inspected family has a Texas production title containing pipeline, so requiring that title would create a false unavailability condition.
